protocol: feedback-validation study v2 (research/astra/feedback_validation_20261003): plate-disjoint design after second-agent review
written_at: first draft 2026-10-03 about 21:30 +0800 (overwritten; exact time not preserved); revised 21:52:00 +0800 (file mtime) after the adversarial review; timestamps corrected 21:54 because earlier typed values (22:05, 22:50) were estimates, not clock readings
question: Does updating a world model with a small number of target-line measurements produce more independently validated discoveries than the strongest static alternative under matched information and well budgets?

status_of_data.primary: UNTOUCHED: Jaaks et al. 2022 Nature 603:166 anchored screen, figshare 16843597, original_screen_all_tissues_fitted.csv (sha256 1188968ce7fdcfb66d03791cf266515b7c7a2794e1fc73c966dba40266ffa278); secondary S11 uses the authors' validation rescreen, figshare 16843600, validation_screen_all_tissues_fitted.csv (sha256 dcbd4c3108d212fa771c52ae977c8e1c01a421162a2232cdc4273faf257b2775).
seen_before_freeze: Header rows of both files and the figshare glossary (anchored_screen_glossary.xlsx).
Design columns only (BARCODE, COMBI_ID, Tissue, CELL_LINE_NAME, SIDM, ANCHOR_ID/NAME/CONC, LIBRARY_ID/NAME/CONC): WS1 census receipts step3f/step3g.

One data row was printed by accident while reading the header (Breast, CAL-120, combination 1022:1005, anchor 0.25 uM: SYNERGY_DELTA_EMAX 0.204, SYNERGY_XMID 10.85, Synergy FALSE). Disclosed; no other outcome value was read.
Jaaks et al. 2022 Methods (PMC8891012): synergy rule, anchor design, single replicate, validation rescreen, synergy rates 5.2% overall (pancreas 7.2%, colon 5.4%, breast 4.4%).
Development evidence: O'Neil 2016 (exposed) and NCI-ALMANAC 2017 (exposed since 2026-10-03T17:58:48) analyses by workstreams WS1-WS4 and the O'Neil parity stage results/dev_oneil_parity.

Plate structure from design columns (BARCODE, Tissue, SIDM, ANCHOR_ID, LIBRARY_ID, ANCHOR_CONC): 3,106 plates, each one cell line with 22-26 anchors and a fixed doublet of 1-2 library drugs; doublets recur across lines (13 in colon and pancreas, about 26 in breast).
status_of_data.exploratory: NCI-ALMANAC (E1) is exposed; its analysis is exploratory and has no verdict.

primary_panel.qc: drop rows with SYNERGY_RMSE > 0.2 or LIBRARY_RMSE > 0.2 (authors' rule) or missing Synergy / SYNERGY_DELTA_EMAX / SYNERGY_OBS_EMAX; counts recorded
primary_panel.calls: authors' rule: per anchor concentration synergistic if >= half of replicate rows have Synergy TRUE; ordered combination synergistic in a line if so at either anchor concentration (strict majority > half: sensitivity S14)
primary_panel.split: per tissue, library doublets (connected components of library drugs sharing plates, from design rows before QC) sorted, permuted by numpy default_rng([20261003, tissue_code]); first floor(n/2) -> S, rest -> V
primary_panel.replicates: SV: screen = S drug anchored, V drug titrated (V-library plates); validation = V drug anchored, S drug titrated (S-library plates). VS: roles swapped on the same menu. Each line's value = mean of SV and VS.
primary_panel.label: screen y = 100 x max over anchor concentrations of mean SYNERGY_DELTA_EMAX (screen orientation); learning and ranking only
primary_panel.menu: S x V pairs with both orientations present after QC, per line; all three tissues
primary_panel.history: other lines of the same tissue, screen orientation of the same replicate only
primary_panel.cost_unit: 14 combination wells x screen plates per purchase; shared single-agent and control wells uncharged (unknown); days per round not recorded (elapsed time in rounds)

arms.history_mean: pair's shrunk mean screen label in other lines (static retrieval)
arms.history_rate: pair's shrunk screen-call rate in other lines, ties by history_mean (static retrieval)
arms.ridge_static: frozen TransferWorld prior, context off, no feedback (static transfer model)
arms.gbm_static: HistGradientBoostingRegressor(max_iter=200, learning_rate=0.1, random_state=0) on the same history features (static transfer model)
arms.feedback: ridge prior + frozen in-context EB posterior (line offset + drug-in-line effects), posterior-mean ranking  <- PRIMARY FEEDBACK ARM
arms.offset_only: ridge prior + posterior line offset only (analytic expectation: identical purchases to ridge_static)
arms.shuffle: feedback arm fed its residuals permuted among the experiments bought in the same round of the same line (10 seeds); breaks drug-outcome pairing, keeps the round's residual distribution and sum
arms.rate_feedback: TransferWorld on the 0/100 screen-call label, prior = shrunk pair call rate in other lines (history_rate's score), plus in-context posterior (EB variances fitted on that label)
arms.wrong_line: feedback arm fed the same pairs' screen labels from one randomly chosen other line of the same panel (10 seeds); breaks target-line specificity, keeps realistic pair structure

budgets.primary: ceil(0.20 x menu) purchases in 4 equal rounds (menu about 169 pairs per line, so about 34 purchases, matching the pre-revision plan of 10% of about 325 pairs)

campaign: frozen agent._top selection with seeded tie-break (seed = line index; random arm seed = its seed); exploit terminal round; no certification branch
primary_endpoint: validated discoveries per line = purchased experiments with a screen-orientation synergy call AND a validation-orientation synergy call
primary_contrast: feedback minus static* (static arm with the most validated discoveries; re-selected in every bootstrap resample). A stop category also requires agreement against history_rate (development winner).
inference: unit = target cell line (mean of SV and VS); percentile bootstrap over lines stratified by tissue, 10,000 resamples, seed 20261003; G = ratio of sums; S13 two-way bootstrap over lines and pairs

meaningful_gain.value: G >= 0.10 (10% more validated discoveries than static*)
justification: Elapsed time: feedback needs 4 sequential assay rounds; any static arm can buy its whole budget in one round, so feedback multiplies campaign duration by about 4 at equal wells.

Development: on O'Neil (screen labels) feedback beat the strongest static arm (history_rate) by +15.4% [6.9, 25.3] (results/dev_oneil_parity); on exposed ALMANAC the comparable gain was +2.0%; WS2's independent single-agent re-scoring on O'Neil removed most of the gain over retrieval (+2.05 -> +0.17 per line) and WS1 estimated that about half of the in-context signal is batch specific.

A 10% bar asks that roughly two thirds of the most favourable development gain survive independent validation; below it, the gain would not in our judgment repay a 4x longer campaign. It was set before any primary outcome was read and is not tuned.

At the revised 20% budget the O'Neil development gain on screen labels is +9.2% [2.6, 16.9] (results/dev_oneil_parity_v2), so the 10% bar is demanding: it asks feedback to do at least as well on independent validation as it did on its own screen labels in development. The bar is kept because the practical cost (4x elapsed time) does not depend on the budget; a SMALL_GAIN would still be reported as a real effect.

verdict_rules.MEANINGFUL_GAIN: G lower bound > 0 and G >= 0.10 -> continue the feedback component
verdict_rules.SMALL_GAIN: G lower bound > 0 and G < 0.10 -> modify: real but below the practical bar; weigh elapsed time
verdict_rules.INCONCLUSIVE: G lower bound <= 0 and upper bound >= 0.10 -> not proof of no effect; more independent units needed before any claim
verdict_rules.NO_MEANINGFUL_GAIN: G lower bound <= 0 and 0 < upper bound < 0.10 -> stop claiming validated-discovery value for feedback in this design
verdict_rules.screen_vs_validation: if S1 (screen hits) shows a gain but the primary does not, investigate noisy feedback and verification allocation before adding complexity; if S4 shows shuffle ~ feedback, inspect shortcuts
verdict_rules.stop_guard: NO_MEANINGFUL_GAIN or HARM against static* stands only if the contrast against history_rate is also NO_MEANINGFUL_GAIN or HARM; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE

secondary.S1: screen hits: feedback minus best static by screen hits (lower-tier, primary-screen yield on an untouched screen)
secondary.S1b: validated: feedback minus each static arm
secondary.S2: validation rate (validated / screen hits) of feedback, static*, shuffle, random
secondary.S3: mean validation label of purchases, feedback minus static* (continuous response)
secondary.S4: feedback minus shuffle; shuffle minus static*
secondary.S6: validated and efficacious (validation-orientation combination viability <= 0.5 at the top library dose, best anchor) discoveries
secondary.S8: budget10 sensitivity of the primary contrast
secondary.S9: feedback on a retrieval prior and on the GBM prior vs their static versions (their EB variances are fitted on ridge residuals: shrinkage mis-specified)
secondary.S11: authors' validation rescreen (selective: author-chosen pairs x lines, different concentrations, separate plates): rescreen synergy rate among purchased experiments in its menu, by arm (descriptive)
secondary.S12: rate_feedback minus history_rate (feedback on the endpoint's own label)
secondary.S13: two-way bootstrap (lines x pairs) interval of G

exploratory_E1.validation: label re-referenced to single agents of the same screener, drug, line and concentration from a test date different from every test date of the experiment's own combination records (NCI's SCORE uses same-plate or same-date companion singles: receipts/reference_design.json); experiment label = mean over records, missing unless every record is covered; validation call = re-referenced label > 10; combination wells shared
exploratory_E1.arms: same arms and primary budget as the Jaaks panels, context off
exploratory_E1.outputs: same estimates as the primary (labelled exploratory, no verdict) plus mean (screen label - reference label) over purchases by arm

dependencies_and_scope: Campaigns in one tissue share the drug library and use each other's screen data as history; lines are therefore not fully independent, and the bootstrap over lines does not model this.

Validation is a second measurement of the same pair in the same lab and campaign, on disjoint plates with the roles of the drugs swapped (own single-agent references); it is not a cross-lab or in vivo replication.
Inference scope: breast, colon and pancreas cell lines of this screen, its drug library and anchor concentrations; new lines screened with the same library.
execution: python -m research.astra.feedback_validation_20261003.run --stage jaaks --out results/jaaks_primary (vault: release, then after the campaigns the rescreen)

Each stage runs once. A crash before outputs may be fixed only in code that does not define arms, endpoints or rules, recorded as a deviation; every vault opening is logged in protocol/vault_log.jsonl.
provider_spend: none planned for this study (WS4 diagnostic spent USD 0.2171 separately)

review.reviewer: second subagent, read-only, about 21:35-21:45 +0800 (no outcome values read)
review.blocking_issue_fixed: a per-pair orientation coin left screen and validation measurements of different pairs on the same plates (shared library-drug reference and plate effects, which in-context drug effects could exploit); replaced by a seeded split of library doublets into S and V so screen plates (V library) and validation plates (S library) are disjoint; asserted per line (PLATE_OVERLAP refusal)
other_changes: learner on the screen call itself (rate_feedback) vs history_rate (S12)
static* re-selected inside every bootstrap resample; stop verdicts also require the pre-specified comparator history_rate
two-way line x pair bootstrap sensitivity (S13)
swap replicate VS on the same menu, averaged with SV per line
vault tickets must match registered data digests
ALMANAC: undated singles cannot count as off-date; validation rate among non-missing

precision_forecast: about +/-8-9 percentage points on G (125 lines, a few validated discoveries per line); the 10% bar is resolvable only if the true gain is about 15% or more, so INCONCLUSIVE is a likely outcome and must not be read as no effect
